name: dead-reckoning
title: Dead Reckoning
description: A 404 rendered as a navigator's chart — the user's real in-app trail plotted as position fixes with bearing lines and time ticks, projected one leg further to an X marked 'position doubtful' at the URL that failed, then a compass rose settles and a corrected course draws itself back to real waypoints (the nearest section, search, home), each a charted, clickable exit.
instruction: Build a full 404 page whose graphic is computed from the user's genuine navigation trail rather than decorating the error. A prop `trail` (array of `{ label, tick? }`, oldest first) supplies the last few in-app steps; absent that, the component tries `window.history.state.trail` (an app can write this via `history.replaceState`), then a same-origin `document.referrer` (titleized last path segment as a single-step trail), and only then falls back to a generic three-waypoint chart (Home / Dashboard / Reports) — so the artwork degrades gracefully instead of rendering empty. Each trail step is plotted as a position fix (small filled circle, Geist Mono label + optional relative time tick beneath) on an SVG graticule grid spaced on the 4px rhythm (stroke --border). Consecutive fixes are joined by dashed dead-reckoning bearing lines in --muted with small perpendicular tick marks, and the track is extended one further leg — by continuing the last bearing — to an X mark in --foreground labeled 'position doubtful' and the attempted URL (prop `attemptedPath`, defaulting to the current location). On mount, a small compass rose (its own corner SVG, N/E/S/W ticks and a two-tone needle) overshoots into place and spring-settles (~620ms, back-eased). Once the doubtful fix is established, a corrected course draws itself leg by leg in --foreground from the X to each of the supplied `exits` (`{ label, href? }`, source order — defaults to Back to Dashboard / Search / Home) via stroke-dashoffset over ~900ms ease-out-expo, staggered per leg, each terminating in a labeled waypoint circle. Those on-chart waypoints are mouse-clickable (tabIndex=-1, sitting inside the aria-hidden figure) but the real 404 page is the plain, visible, focusable link list rendered below the chart in the same source order, hovering or focusing one of which highlights its matching chart waypoint in --accent — the only non-interaction use of color stays out of the chart itself. The h1 reads exactly '404 — page not found'. Reduced motion renders the whole chart already drawn: no compass settle, no stroke-dashoffset reveal, no fix drop-in.
